reason: The analysis implementation and adversarial synthetic tests are pinned before any raw tool-call argument is parsed. Initial preregistration attempts and the first test failure are retained in sanitized failure logs.

Adversarial code review found the first replay did not reject drift in unselected source-record bytes even though all selected rows were hash-checked. Added a source-snapshot and selected-multiset gate plus a tamper counterexample. The first outputs are preserved unchanged at their original paths; the corrected replay writes to a versioned directory and must reproduce the finite counts or classify source drift as INVALID_EXPERIMENT.

Adversarial reporting review found the v2 aggregate omitted counts of evidence-reference equality by permission. Add those counts to a separately versioned v3 export; this is a reporting-completeness change only. The fixed 48-pair schedule and already parsed raw predictions are unchanged; v1/v2 artifacts remain preserved.

An independent critic found the parser replay did not independently enforce the externally registered schedule SHA, exact 24/24 permission denominators, or duplicate request-ID rejection. Added all three gates and counterexample tests. Also restored the selector source byte-for-byte to the preregistered SHA; the earlier test repair is now isolated to synthetic fixture construction by supplying inert, unselected attempt rows up to the frozen source count. Rebuilt schedule exactly matches the registered schedule hash. v1-v3 outputs and all initial failure records remain unchanged; v4 is a new zero-call replay.

reason: A second independent review found audit_pairs accepted an arbitrary in-memory schedule dict even though the CLI checked the frozen file, and duplicate-ID tests covered only current results. Made the public audit API accept a schedule path and enforce the preregistered SHA before reading; retained the dictionary audit as an internal unit-test helper. Added tests for replacement schedules, duplicate historical prediction IDs, and duplicate attempt IDs. The v4 output remains unchanged; v5 will be a new replay with an explicit frozen_schedule_verified field.
